name: Lateral Collateral Ligament / Posterolateral Corner Injury
definition: Injury of the lateral collateral ligament and/or posterolateral corner, often from varus or rotational trauma and frequently associated with cruciate injury.

investigations.principle: MRI helps define complex soft-tissue injury.
investigations.MRI: MRI is preferred for suspected PLC injury.

amber: High-grade or combined PLC injuries often require early orthopedic evaluation.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Janu-sandhi/Snayu injury phenotype may be documented.

patientEducation.summary: Injury of the lateral collateral ligament and/or posterolateral corner, often from varus or rotational trauma and frequently associated with cruciate injury.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for severe/progressive neurological deficit, vascular compromise, infection/systemic illness, major trauma, sphincter change or other listed red flags.
